'''Marco Asensio Willemsen''' ({{IPA|es|ˈmaɾko aˈsensjo|lang}}; born 21 January 1996) is a Spanish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Winger (association football)|winger]] or [[attacking midfielder]] for [[Süper Lig]] club [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (football)|Fenerbahçe]].

After starting his career with [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]], Asensio signed for [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in November 2014, being consecutively loaned to his former club as well as [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]]. With Real Madrid, he went on to win several honours, including three [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] and three [[La Liga]] trophies. In 2023, he joined French club [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]]. Following a one-season loan stint in the [[Premier League]] with [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] in 2025, Asensio then transferred to Turkish club Fenerbahçe.

Asensio made his senior debut for Spain in 2016, representing them at the [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018]] and [[2022 FIFA World Cup]].

==Early life==
Born in [[Palma de Mallorca|Palma]], [[Majorca]], [[Balearic Islands]], to a Dutch mother and a Spanish father,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.diariodemallorca.es/rcd-mallorca/2014/08/27/seguido-meses-elite-europea/957496.html#.WvF3Ai7wdPdgguL|title=Seguido desde hace meses por la élite europe|trans-title=Followed by the European elite for months|newspaper=Diario de Mallorca|language=es|date=27 August 2014|access-date=1 December 2014}}</ref><ref name=Dreamed>{{cite news|url=https://en.as.com/en/2016/10/22/football/1477131768_167624.html|title=Asensio's father dreamed his son would play for Athletic Club|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|date=22 October 2016|access-date=15 October 2018|archive-date=10 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210510072142/https://en.as.com/en/2016/10/22/football/1477131768_167624.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> Asensio joined [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]] in 2006 from [[CF Platges de Calvià B|Platges de Calvià]]. His mother, Maria Willemsen, died of cancer when he was 15.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://okdiario.com/real-madrid/futbol/primer-equipo/2016/08/16/asensio-no-pudo-contener-lagrimas-recordar-madre-37274|title=Asensio no pudo retener las lágrimas al recordar a su madre|trans-title=Asensio could not hold back the tears when remembering his mother|publisher=OK Diario|language=es|date=16 August 2016|access-date=16 August 2017}}</ref> Asensio struggled with growth deficiencies in his knees during his youth, which only subsided when he was a teenager.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://donbalonrosa.defensacentral.com/el-grave-problema-que-sufrio-marco-asensio-en-su-infancia|title=El grave problema que sufrió Marco Asensio en su infancia|trans-title=The serious problem from which Marco Asensio suffered in his youth|publisher=Don Balón Rosa|language=es|date=10 May 2017|access-date=16 August 2017}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Mallorca===
After being scouted by [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] and [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.diariodemallorca.es/deportes/2013/02/25/madrid-barca-pugnan-asensio/828920.html|title=Madrid y Barça pugnan por Asensio|trans-title=Madrid and Barça fight for Asensio|newspaper=Diario de Mallorca|language=es|date=25 February 2013|access-date=18 November 2013}}</ref> Asensio made his senior debut with [[RCD Mallorca B|Mallorca's reserves]] in the [[2013–14 Tercera División|2013–14 season]] in the [[Tercera División]], despite still being a junior; he made his first competitive appearance for the first team on 27 October 2013, playing the last six minutes in a 1–3 away loss against [[Recreativo de Huelva]] in the [[Segunda División]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2013/10/27/futbol/2adivision/1382878841.html|title=Linares reafirma el liderato del Decano|trans-title=Linares confirms first place for the Dean|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=es|date=27 October 2013|access-date=18 November 2013}}</ref>

Again [[Substitute (association football)|from the bench]], Asensio played the last six minutes in a 0–0 home draw against [[CD Lugo|Lugo]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2013/11/02/futbol/2adivision/1383420718.html|title=Los lucenses tiran de oficio para resistir en el Iberostar|trans-title=''Lucences'' resort to know-how to resist at Iberostar|newspaper=Marca|location=Spain|language=es|date=2 November 2013|access-date=18 November 2013}}</ref> After impressing in his first games, he was promoted to the first team by manager [[José Luis Oltra]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://ultimahora.es/mallorca/noticia/deportes/real-mallorca/marco-asensio-llama-puerta.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20131118184225/http://ultimahora.es/mallorca/noticia/deportes/real-mallorca/marco-asensio-llama-puerta.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=18 November 2013|title=Marco Asensio llama a la puerta|trans-title=Marco Asensio knocks on the door|newspaper=[[Última Hora (Spain)|Última Hora]]|language=es|date=4 November 2013|access-date=18 November 2013}}</ref> Asensio scored his first professional goal on 16 March 2014, netting the first in a 2–0 home win over [[CD Tenerife|Tenerife]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2014/03/16/futbol/2adivision/1394996127.html|title=Asensio y Thomas dan aire a los baleares ante un flojo Tenerife|trans-title=Asensio and Thomas give air to the Balearic against a weak Tenerife|newspaper=Marca|location=Spain|language=es|date=16 March 2014|access-date=13 July 2014}}</ref> The next season he was made a starter under new coach [[Valeri Karpin]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2014/10/27/futbol/equipos/mallorca/1414411032.html|title=Los imprescindibles de Karpin|trans-title=Karpin's undisputed|newspaper=Marca|location=Spain|language=es|date=27 October 2014|access-date=2 May 2016}}</ref> scoring against [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.abc.es/deportes/futbol/20140921/abci-osasuna-mallorca-goles-201409211415.html|title=Osasuna y Mallorca firman otro aluvión de goles: 6–4|trans-title=Osasuna and Mallorca sign another goal flood: 6–4|newspaper=[[ABC (newspaper)|ABC]]|language=es|date=21 September 2014|access-date=2 May 2016}}</ref> [[Deportivo Alavés]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.mundodeportivo.com/20141011/futbol/2-0-marco-asensio-salva-del-despido-a-karpin_54417012218.html|title=2–0: Marco Asensio salva del despido a Karpin|trans-title=2–0: Marco Asensio prevents sacking of Karpin|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|language=es|date=11 October 2014|access-date=2 May 2016}}</ref> and [[CF Badalona Futur|Llagostera]] within a month.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.diariodemallorca.es/rcd-mallorca/2014/10/19/directo-llagostera---mallorca/970008.html|title=El Mallorca golea al Llagostera y sale del descenso|trans-title=Mallorca rout Llagostera and leave relegation zone|newspaper=Diario de Mallorca|language=es|date=19 October 2014|access-date=2 May 2016}}</ref>

===Real Madrid===
On 24 November 2014, Real Madrid reached an agreement in principle to sign 18-year-old Asensio.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/en/2014/11/24/en/football/real_madrid/1416830153.html|title=Marco Asensio, Bernabéu-bound|newspaper=Marca|location=Spain|date=24 November 2014|access-date=25 November 2014}}</ref> On 5 December the deal was officially announced, with the player (who had been a supporter of the club as a child)<ref name=Dreamed/> signing a six-year deal for a €3.9&nbsp;million fee<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2014/12/05/futbol/equipos/real_madrid/1417792389.html|title=Marco Asensio, al Real Madrid por 3,9 millones|trans-title=Marco Asensio, to Real Madrid for 3.9&nbsp;million|newspaper=Marca|location=Spain|language=es|date=5 December 2014|access-date=5 December 2014}}</ref> and remaining with the ''Bermellones'' on loan until the end of [[2014–15 Segunda División|the campaign]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/12/official-announcement-marco-asensio|title=Official announcement: Marco Asensio|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=5 December 2014|access-date=5 December 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rcdmallorca.es/principal_new.php?nombreModulo=noticiasDetalle&idnoticia=33964&idmenu=3 |title=Mallorca y Madrid cierran el traspaso de Marco Asensio|trans-title=Mallorca and Madrid complete the transfer of Marco Asensio|publisher=RCD Mallorca|language=es|date=5 December 2014|access-date=2 March 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141208172526/http://www.rcdmallorca.es/principal_new.php?nombreModulo=noticiasDetalle&idnoticia=33964&idmenu=3|archive-date=8 December 2014}}</ref> According to Real Madrid president [[Florentino Pérez]], Spanish tennis player [[Rafael Nadal]] played a crucial role in the transfer of Marco Asensio to Real Madrid.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/european/real-madrid-transfer-news-marco-asensio-rafael-nadal-helped-florentino-perez-a7798996.html|title=How Rafael Nadal helped Real Madrid sign Marco Asensio|date=20 June 2017|website=The Independent|access-date=11 January 2019}}</ref>

====2015–16 season: Loan to Espanyol====
On 20 August 2015, after making the whole pre-season with Real Madrid, Asensio was loaned to [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] in [[La Liga]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/08/official-announcement-marco-asensio|title=Official announcement: Marco Asensio|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=20 August 2015|access-date=20 August 2015}}</ref> He played his first game in the competition on 19 September, featuring 86 minutes in a 3–2 success at [[Real Sociedad]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/rcd-espanyol/20150919/201775146000/2-3-el-espanyol-se-rehabilita-en-anoeta.html|title=El Espanyol se rehabilita en Anoeta|trans-title=Espanyol rehabilitate in Anoeta|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|language=es|date=19 September 2015|access-date=2 May 2016}}</ref> and he ended his spell at the [[RCDE Stadium|Estadi Cornellà-El Prat]] with 12 overall [[Assist (football)|assists]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2016/03/17/primera/1458203456_171382.html|title=Asensio crece en el Espanyol: está en el Top-10 de asistencias|trans-title=Asensio grows in Espanyol: he makes Top-10 in assists|newspaper=Diario AS|language=es|date=17 March 2016|access-date=10 August 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2016/05/31/primera/1464713838_662484.html|title=El Espanyol colgará el cuadro de su internacional 43: Asensio|trans-title=Espanyol will hang its 43rd international in the rafters: Asensio|newspaper=Diario AS|language=es|date=1 June 2016|access-date=10 August 2016}}</ref>

====2016–17 season: Return to Real Madrid====
Returning to the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium]] for [[2016–17 La Liga|2016–17]], Asensio was now a full international. His first competitive appearance took place on 9 August, as he played the full 120 minutes and scored a 25-meter effort in a [[2016 UEFA Super Cup|3–2 win]] against fellow Spaniards [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] in the [[UEFA Super Cup]].<ref name="ESPN">{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.co.uk/report?gameId=450351|title=Dani Carvajal's late goal in ET helps Real Madrid win UEFA Super Cup|publisher=[[ESPN FC]]|date=9 August 2016|access-date=9 August 2016}}</ref> He made his first league start 12 days later, netting the second goal in a 3–0 success at Real Sociedad.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2016/08/21/primera/1471809433_290537.html|title=Morata y Marco Asensio modernizan al Real Madrid|trans-title=Morata and Marco Asensio modernise Real Madrid|newspaper=Diario AS|language=es|date=21 August 2016|access-date=21 August 2016}}</ref>

Asensio featured 23 times over [[2016–17 Real Madrid CF season|his first season]], scoring three times<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2016_17/la-liga/jornada_6/pal_rma/|title=Fiebre amarilla|trans-title=Yellow fever|newspaper=Marca|location=Spain|language=es|date=24 September 2016|access-date=22 May 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.lavanguardia.com/deportes/futbol/20170304/42539634788/eibar-real-madrid-resumen.html|title=El Madrid se pasea en Eibar|trans-title=Madrid go sightseeing in Eibar|newspaper=[[La Vanguardia]]|language=es|date=4 March 2017|access-date=22 May 2017}}</ref> as the club won the national championship for the first time since 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.laliga.es/noticias/real-madrid-campeon-de-laliga-santander-2016-17|title=El Real Madrid, campeón de LaLiga Santander 2016/17|trans-title=Real Madrid, LaLiga Santander champions 2016/17|publisher=[[La Liga]]|language=es|date=21 May 2017|access-date=22 May 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/39926301|title=Malaga 0–2 Real Madrid|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=21 May 2017|access-date=22 May 2017}}</ref> He added as many goals in [[2016–17 UEFA Champions League|that year]]'s [[UEFA Champions League]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/37671862|title=Real Madrid 5–1 Legia Warsaw|work=BBC Sport|date=18 October 2016|access-date=6 June 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/39611654|title=Real Madrid 4–2 Bayern Munich|work=BBC Sport|date=18 April 2017|access-date=6 June 2017}}</ref> including one in [[2017 UEFA Champions League Final|the final]] against [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] (4–1) to give the Spaniards their 12th title in the latter competition.<ref name="UEFA">{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0250-0c5117c008df-de0901ea6dae-1000--majestic-real-madrid-win-champions-league-in-cardiff/|title=Majestic Real Madrid win Champions League in Cardiff|publisher=UEFA|date=3 June 2017|access-date=4 June 2017}}</ref>

====2017–18 season====
[[File:Asensio 2018 (cropped).jpg|left|thumb|180px|upright|Asensio playing for Real Madrid against [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] in 2018]]
Asensio scored his first goal of the [[2017–18 Real Madrid CF season|2017–18 season]] with a 25-yard finish in a [[2017 Supercopa de España|3–1 win]] over Barcelona at the [[Camp Nou]], for the [[Supercopa de España]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/spanish-super-cup/431/blog/post/3179259/cristiano-ronaldo-sent-off-but-real-madrid-easily-beat-barcelona-in-spanish-super-cup|title=Cristiano Ronaldo sent off but Real Madrid easily beat Barcelona|publisher=ESPN FC|date=13 August 2017|access-date=14 August 2017}}</ref> He repeated the feat with a similarly spectacular effort in the second leg, in a 5–1 aggregate triumph.<ref name="TELEGRAPH">{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2017/08/16/real-madrid-vs-barcelona-spanish-super-cup-live-score-updates/|title=Real Madrid 2 Barcelona 0 (5–1 on aggregate): Woeful Barca dismissed as Zinedine Zidane's unstoppable side win Super Cup|newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|date=16 August 2017|access-date=17 August 2017}}</ref>

On 28 September 2017, Asensio extended his contract until 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2017/09/ceremony-to-mark-asensios-contract-renewal|title=Ceremony to mark Asensio's contract renewal|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=28 September 2017|access-date=28 September 2017}}</ref> On 18 February 2018, in a match where he contributed with a brace to a 5–3 away win over [[Real Betis]], he scored Real Madrid's 6,000th goal in the [[Spanish football league system|Spanish top division]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sport.es/es/noticias/real-madrid/doblete-asensio-gol-6000-del-madrid-liga-6633442|title=Doblete de Asensio y gol 6000 del Madrid en la Liga|trans-title=Asensio brace and goal 6000 from Madrid in League|newspaper=[[Sport (Spanish newspaper)|Sport]]|language=es|date=18 February 2018|access-date=18 February 2018}}</ref> Asensio made 11 appearances while scoring one goal during the [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League|2017–18 Champions League]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rcnradio.com/deportes/asi-llegan-las-plantillas-de-real-madrid-y-liverpool-la-final-de-la-champions|title=Así llegan Real Madrid y Liverpool a la final de la Champions|trans-title=That is how Real Madrid and Liverpool arrive to the Champions final|publisher=[[RCN Radio]]|language=es|date=25 May 2018|access-date=29 May 2018}}</ref> and the club won its third consecutive and 13th overall title in the competition.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0245-0e98d7318379-716954065574-1000--madrid-beat-liverpool-to-complete-hat-trick/|title=Madrid beat Liverpool to complete hat-trick|publisher=UEFA|date=26 May 2018|access-date=28 May 2018}}</ref>

====2019–2023: Final seasons ====
[[File:Ofrenda de la Liga y la Champions-22-L.Millán (52109789880).jpg|thumb|300x300px|upright|Asensio in trophy presentation ceremony at [[Virgin of Almudena]] in 2022]]
On 24 July 2019, during a preseason match against [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], he tore his [[Anterior cruciate ligament injury|ACL]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2019/07/24/5d3841ac268e3e490d8b45e8.html|title=Real Madrid confirm Asensio's ACL injury |work=Marca|location=Spain |date=24 July 2019|access-date=24 July 2019}}</ref> On 19 June 2020, in a 3–0 win over [[Valencia CF|Valencia]], he came on for [[Federico Valverde]] in 74th minute, scored the second goal with his first touch, and provided the assist to [[Karim Benzema]] for the third goal.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kirkland |first=Alex|date=18 June 2020|title=Benzema's brace earns him 9/10 as Real Madrid stroll vs. Valencia|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/real-madrid/story/4115447/benzemas-brace-earns-him-9-10-as-real-madrid-stroll-while-asensios-comeback-cameo-steals-the-show|publisher=ESPN}}</ref> He returned for the final stretch of the season, scoring three goals in nine games, as Real Madrid won the [[2019–20 La Liga]].<ref name=Liga>{{cite web |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2020/07/17/5f10db2146163f3c2c8b45d7.html|title=Real Madrid win the longest LaLiga Santander season|date=17 July 2020|access-date=17 July 2020|website=Marca|location=Spain}}</ref> On 22 September 2021, he scored his first senior hat-trick against his former club [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]], which ended in a 6–1 victory.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Football news – Marcos Asensio and Karim Benzema star as Real Madrid rout Mallorca to go top of La Liga|date=22 September 2021 |url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/liga/2021-2022/football-news-real-madrid-v-rcd-mallorca-follow-live_sto8550530/story.shtml|access-date=22 September 2021|publisher=eurosport.com}}</ref>

On 28 May 2022, Asensio was on the bench against [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] in the UEFA Champions League Final as Real Madrid went on to win their 14th [[UEFA Champions League]] title.<ref name="CL21">{{cite news |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0275-15415a62aaf0-36d3e17d7404-1000/ |title=Champions League final: Vinícius Júnior scores only goal as Real Madrid deny Liverpool again |publisher=UEFA |date=28 May 2022 |access-date=28 May 2022}}</ref> Asensio ended the 2021–22 season with 10 goals in 30 [[La Liga]] games. He also won the [[2021–22 La Liga]] with his club Real Madrid.<ref name="Liga21">{{cite web |last=Westwood |first=James |date=30 April 2022 |title=Real Madrid clinch 35th La Liga title with four games to spare after victory over Espanyol |url=https://www.goal.com/en-us/news/real-madrid-35th-la-liga-title/bltb8dfbd27f32f5feb |access-date=30 April 2022 |website=Goal (website)}}</ref> On 3 June 2023, Real Madrid confirmed that Asensio would be departing upon the expiry of his contract, thus becoming a free agent.<ref>{{cite news|title=Official Announcement: Marco Asensio|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2023/06/03/official-announcement-marco-asensio|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=3 June 2023|access-date=3 June 2023}}</ref>

===Paris Saint-Germain===
On 6 July 2023, [[Ligue 1]] club [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] (PSG) announced the signing of Asensio, with a contract running until June 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |date=6 July 2023 |title=Marco Asensio joins Paris Saint-Germain through to 2026 |url=https://en.psg.fr/teams/first-team/content/marco-asensio-joins-paris-saint-germain-through-to-2026 |access-date=6 July 2023 |website=Paris Saint-Germain F.C.}}</ref> He made his debut in a 0–0 draw against [[FC Lorient|Lorient]] at the [[Parc des Princes]] on 12 August.<ref>{{Cite web |date=12 August 2023 |title=Paris Saint-Germain V Lorient |url=https://en.psg.fr/teams/first-team/fixtures-and-results/202324/paris-saint-germain-v-lorient |access-date=12 August 2023 |publisher=Paris Saint-Germain F.C.}}</ref> Two weeks later, in his second match for the club, Asensio scored his first PSG goal, the opener in a 3–1 home win over [[RC Lens|Lens]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Asensio and Mbappe on target as PSG beat Lens 3-1 |url=https://www.channelnewsasia.com/sport/paris-st-germain-victory-marco-asensio-first-goal-kylian-mbappe-3727231 |access-date=1 October 2023 |website=CNA |language=en}}</ref> In the following match away to [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] on 3 September, he scored another goal and provided the assist for [[Kylian Mbappé]]'s second in a 4–1 victory for ''Les Parisiens''.<ref>{{Cite web |date=14 September 2023 |title=Marco Asensio's early PSG form suggests Real Madrid had an answer to their No.9 problem right under their nose {{!}} Goal.com |url=https://www.goal.com/en/lists/marco-asensio-early-psg-form-suggests-real-madrid-had-answer-their-no-9-problem-right-under-their-nose/bltc992ddf8fe08994e |access-date=1 October 2023 |website=www.goal.com |language=en}}</ref>

====Loan to Aston Villa====
On 3 February 2025, Premier League side Aston Villa announced the loan signing of Asensio until the end of [[2024–25 Premier League|the season]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 February 2025 |title=Villa confirm Marco Asensio loan deal |url=https://www.avfc.co.uk/news/2025/february/03/villa-confirm-marco-asensio-loan-deal/ |access-date=3 February 2025 |website=Aston Villa Football Club}}</ref> He made his debut on 9 February, coming on as a substitute in a 2–1 [[FA Cup]] victory against [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=9 February 2025 |title=What Marco Asensio's Aston Villa Debut Against Tottenham Revealed to British Media |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/marco-asensio-aston-villa-debut-181600535.html |access-date=22 February 2025 |website=British Broadcasting Corporation}}</ref> On 22 February 2025, he scored his first two goals for Villa to give them a 2–1 comeback win over [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] in the league.<ref>{{Cite web |date=22 February 2025 |title=Aston Villa 2–1 Chelsea |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/ckg7g8v5pewt |access-date=22 February 2025 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref>

=== Fenerbahçe ===
On 1 September 2025, Asensio signed for Turkish [[Süper Lig]] club [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (football)|Fenerbahçe]] on a three-year contract with an option for a further year.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ailemize hoş geldin Marco Asensio |url=https://fenerbahce.org/haberler/futbol/2025/8/ailemize-hos-geldin-marco-asensio |date= 2025-09-01 |access-date=2025-09-01 |website=www.Fenerbahçe SK |language=tr}}</ref> A transfer fee of €8.5 million was reported in the media.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-09-01 |title=Official {{!}} Fenerbahçe sign Marco Asensio from PSG - Get French Football News |url=https://www.getfootballnewsfrance.com/2025/official-fenerbahce-sign-marco-asensio-from-psg/ |access-date=2025-09-01 |language=en-US}}</ref> On 14 September, he made his debut with the team in a 1–0 league victory over [[Trabzonspor]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://fenerbahce.org/haberler/futbol/2025/9/fenerbahce-1-0-trabzonspor |title=Fenerbahçe 1-0 Trabzonspor |publisher=Fenerbahçe S.K. |language=tr |date=14 September 2025 }}</ref> On 21 September, he scored his first goal for the club against [[Kasımpaşa S.K.|Kasımpaşa]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://fenerbahce.org/haberler/futbol/2025/9/kasimpasa-1-1-fenerbahce |title=Kasımpaşa 1-1 Fenerbahçe |publisher=Fenerbahçe S.K. |language=tr |date=21 September 2025 }}</ref> On 24 September, he made his [[UEFA Europa League]] debut against [[GNK Dinamo Zagreb|Dinamo Zagreb]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://fenerbahce.org/haberler/futbol/2025/9/gnk-dinamo-zagreb-3-1-fenerbahce |title=GNK Dinamo Zagreb 3-1 Fenerbahçe |publisher=Fenerbahçe S.K. |language=tr |date=24 September 2025 }}</ref> On 2 November, Asensio scored in the [[Beşiktaş–Fenerbahçe rivalry (football)|derby]] against [[Beşiktaş J.K.|Beşiktaş]], helping his side to 3–2 win.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://fenerbahce.org/haberler/futbol/2025/11/besiktas-2-3-fenerbahce |title=Beşiktaş 2-3 Fenerbahçe |publisher=Fenerbahçe S.K. |language=tr |date=2 November 2025 }}</ref> On 23 November, he scored a brace against [[Çaykur Rizespor]], in a 5–2 league win.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://fenerbahce.org/haberler/futbol/2025/11/caykur-rizespor-2-5-fenerbahce | title=Çaykur Rizespor 2-5 Fenerbahçe |date=23 November 2025 |website=fenerbahce.org |language=tr}}</ref> The goals against Çaykur Rizespor meant he had scored in five consecutive matches, a first in Asensio's career.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.turkiyegazetesi.com.tr/spor/fenerbahcede-marco-asensio-sov-kariyerinde-bir-ilke-imza-atti-1595559 | title=Fenerbahçe'de Marco Asensio şov yaptı, 6. golünü attı: Kariyerinde bir ilki başardı |date=23 November 2025 |website=turkiyegazetesi.com.tr |language=tr}}</ref> On 14 February 2026, Asensio scored in another crucial match, scored his 10th [[Süper Lig]] goal against [[Trabzonspor]], helping Fenerbahçe to 3–2 away win.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fenerbahce.org/haberler/futbol/2026/2/trabzonspor-2-3-fenerbahce |title=Trabzonspor 2-3 Fenerbahçe |publisher=Fenerbahçe S.K. |language=tr |date=14 February 2026 }}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:Marco Asensio, UEFA U21 2017 c.jpg|thumb|right|Asensio during a [[2017 UEFA European Under-21 Championship|2017 European Under-21 Championship]] match against [[Portugal national under-21 football team|Portugal]]|253x253px]]
Being of both Dutch and Spanish descent, he chose to represent Spain although he received an invitation from the [[Royal Dutch Football Association]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.besoccer.com/new/marco-asensio-could-have-played-for-holland|title=Marco Asensio could have played for Holland}}</ref> After being a regular for [[Spain national youth football team|Spain at youth level]], Asensio made his debut for the [[Spain national under-21 football team|under-21 team]] on 26 March 2015, coming on as a late substitute for goalscorer [[Gerard Deulofeu]] in a 2–0 [[Exhibition game|friendly]] win over [[Norway national football team|Norway]] in [[Cartagena, Spain|Cartagena]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sefutbol.com/en/report-spain-beats-norway-and-strengthens-team-2-0|title=Spain beats Norway and strengthens the team (2–0)|publisher=[[Royal Spanish Football Federation]]|last=Muñoz|first=Antonio D.|date=26 March 2015|access-date=30 March 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150328194045/http://www.sefutbol.com/en/report-spain-beats-norway-and-strengthens-team-2-0|archive-date=28 March 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> In July, he was part of the victorious [[Spain national under-19 football team|under-19 side]] at the [[2015 UEFA European Under-19 Championship|UEFA European Championship]] in Greece, where he scored both goals in a semi-final victory over [[France national under-19 football team|France]] in [[Katerini]], in the 88th minute and in added time.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/under19/news/0257-0dedb0cd5d46-6806c2c859df-1000--late-asensio-strikes-take-spain-into-final-again/|title=Late Asensio strikes take Spain into final again|publisher=UEFA|last=Haslam|first=Andrew|date=16 July 2015|access-date=29 July 2015}}</ref>

[[File:ESP-RUS (14).jpg|left|thumb|upright|200x200px|Asensio playing for [[Spain national football team|Spain]] in [[2018 FIFA World Cup]] against [[Russia national football team|Russia]]]]
On 17 May 2016, Asensio and Espanyol teammate [[Pau López]] were called up to [[Spain national football team|the full side]] for a [[Exhibition match|friendly]] against [[Bosnia and Herzegovina national football team|Bosnia and Herzegovina]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rcdespanyol.com/es/actualidad/pau-lopez-y-marco-asensio-convocados-por-del-bosque/_n:2915/|title=Pau López y Marco Asensio, convocados por Del Bosque|trans-title=Pau López and Marco Asensio, called up by Del Bosque|publisher=RCD Espanyol|language=es|date=17 May 2016|access-date=29 May 2016}}</ref> The 20-year-old made his debut on the 29th, starting in the 3–1 win in Switzerland.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2015_16/amistosos_seleccion/3/spa_bih/|title=Nolito endulza un duelo atípico|trans-title=Nolito sweetens an atypical duel|newspaper=Marca|location=Spain|language=es|date=29 May 2016|access-date=29 May 2016}}</ref> Selected in the [[2017 UEFA European Under-21 Championship squads#Spain|squad]] for the [[2017 UEFA European Under-21 Championship|2017 European Under-21 Championship]] by manager [[Albert Celades]], Asensio scored a [[hat-trick]] in his debut in the competition, helping to a 5–0 group stage routing of [[Macedonia national under-21 football team|Macedonia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/under21/news/0257-0dee1aa243c8-76063acdd02c-1000--asensio-scores-fifth-u21-euro-finals-hat-trick/|title=Asensio scores fifth U21 EURO finals hat-trick|publisher=UEFA|date=17 June 2017|access-date=18 June 2017}}</ref> He reached with his teammates the [[2017 UEFA European Under-21 Championship Final|final]] of the tournament, losing 1–0 against [[Germany national under-21 football team|Germany]]. Back with the seniors, he was included in [[Julen Lopetegui]]'s [[2018 FIFA World Cup squads#Spain|squad]] for the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/morata-misses-out-on-spain-world-cup-squad/1ub1qz7jod09i1lfvdcy84ea2l|title=Morata misses out on Spain's 23-man World Cup squad|work=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|date=21 May 2018|access-date=21 May 2018}}</ref> making his debut in [[FIFA World Cup|the competition]] on 20 June by replacing Real Madrid teammate [[Lucas Vázquez]] for the final ten minutes of the 1–0 group stage win against [[Iran national football team|Iran]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/aponline/2018/06/20/sports/soccer/ap-soc-wcup-iran-spain.html|title=Diego Costa scores again, Spain beats Iran 1–0 at World Cup|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|date=20 June 2018|access-date=20 June 2018}}</ref>

Asensio scored his first goal for Spain on 11 September 2018, playing the entire 6–0 home rout of [[Croatia national football team|Croatia]] for the [[2018–19 UEFA Nations League|UEFA Nations League]] and also being directly involved in the play that led to [[Lovre Kalinić]]'s [[own goal]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://en.as.com/en/2018/09/11/football/1536687949_030758.html?omnaut=1|title=Spain – Croatia match report: UEFA Nations League|newspaper=Diario AS|last=Dunne|first=Robbie|date=11 September 2018|access-date=11 September 2018|archive-date=12 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180912022014/https://en.as.com/en/2018/09/11/football/1536687949_030758.html?omnaut=1|url-status=dead}}</ref> In July 2021, he was included as overage player in the 22-player squad of the [[Spain national under-23 football team|under-23 team]] for the [[Football at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2020 Summer Olympics]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Estos son los internacionales que representarán a España en Tokio |date=29 June 2021 |url=https://www.sefutbol.com/oficial-estos-son-internacionales-que-representaran-espana-tokio |publisher=SEFutbol |access-date=29 June 2021 |language=es |archive-date=4 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210704000851/https://www.sefutbol.com/oficial-estos-son-internacionales-que-representaran-espana-tokio |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine|agency=Associated Press|title=Spain Names Six From Euro Squad to Olympic Roster|url=https://www.si.com/soccer/2021/06/29/spain-olympics-squad-euro-2020-pedri-dani-olmo|access-date=1 July 2021|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=29 June 2021 |language=en-us}}</ref> In November 2022, Asensio was included in Spain's final 26-man squad for the [[2022 World Cup]]. He started against Costa Rica in the opening fixture of Spain's World Cup campaign, and scored the second goal against Costa Rica which Spain won 7–0.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cardenas |first=Felipe |title=Asensio lights up the most lopsided game in World Cup history |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3928860/2022/11/23/asensio-spain-costa-rica-world-cup/ |access-date=28 February 2023 |website=The Athletic |date=6 December 2022 |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Asensio's father, Gilberto (a [[Basques|Basque]] who spent his childhood in [[Essen]], Germany), was also a footballer.<ref name=Dreamed/> Also an attacking midfielder, Gilberto represented [[Barakaldo CF]] as a youth;<ref name=Dreamed/> Marco's elder brother Igor played for [[CF Platges de Calvià|Platges de Calvià]], as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2014/10/14/futbol/equipos/mallorca/1413275888.html|title=Marco Asensio, la joya mileurista|trans-title=Marco Asensio, the ''mileurista'' pearl|newspaper=Marca|location=Spain|language=es|date=14 October 2014|access-date=16 August 2017}}</ref> Asensio's [[goal celebration]] in the 2017 Champions League final was dedicated to his family: "I told them that if I scored then I'd run to where they were. I knew where they were and that is what I did."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2018/10/11/5bbf29a0e2704e765e8b45e1.html|title=Asensio returns to Cardiff, a city of happy memories|newspaper=Marca|location=Spain|last1=Lara|first1=Miguel Ángel|last2=McTear|first2=Euan|date=11 October 2018|access-date=12 October 2018}}</ref>

Asensio holds dual Spanish–Dutch citizenship<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-02-19 |title=Asensio speaks Dutch with his grandmother |url=https://www.realtotal.de/en/video/asensio-spricht-hollaendisch-mit-seiner-oma/ |access-date=2025-07-30 |website=REAL TOTAL |language=en}}</ref> and is [[multilingual]], being a native speaker of both [[Spanish language|Spanish]] and [[Dutch language|Dutch]] while also speaking fluent [[German language|German]], [[English language|English]] and [[Catalan language|Catalan]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-04-05 |title=What next for Real Madrid starlet Asensio as Espanyol loan comes to an end? |url=https://www.sport.es/en/news/laliga/what-next-for-real-madrid-5135059 |access-date=2025-09-14 |website=Sports.es |language=en}}</ref>

Asensio married architect, interior designer and entrepreneur Sandra Garal on 7 July 2023 after five years of dating.<ref>{{Cite web |title= Las fotografías oficiales del enlace de Marco Asensio y Sandra Garal en una espectacular fortaleza de Mallorca |url= https://www.hola.com/actualidad/20230829237961/ultima-celebracion-sandra-garal-marco-asensio-tras-boda/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230830021247/https://www.hola.com/actualidad/20230829237961/ultima-celebracion-sandra-garal-marco-asensio-tras-boda/  |archive-date=30 August 2023 |url-status=live |first=Carla |last=Calvo |date=30 August 2023 |access-date=10 October 2026 |website=[[!Hola!]] |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Sandra Garal, de arquitecta a empresaria beauty: “Mi firma tenía que ser de marca España y vegana” |url= https://www.vanitatis.elconfidencial.com/famosos/2025-03-23/sandra-garal-ceo-de-sainte-beauty-lasociedad-sigue-limitando-a-mujeres-como-simples-parejas-de_4089730/ |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20250323054245/https://www.vanitatis.elconfidencial.com/famosos/2025-03-23/sandra-garal-ceo-de-sainte-beauty-lasociedad-sigue-limitando-a-mujeres-como-simples-parejas-de_4089730/ |archive-date=23 March 2025 |url-status=live |first=Berenice |last=Lobatón |date=23 March 2025 |access-date=10 October 2026 |website=Vanitatis |language=es}}</ref> In June 2024, Asensio and Garal announced on their respective social media confirming a mutual agreement to divorce.<ref>{{cite news |last=B |first=James |date=11 June 2024 |title=Marco Asensio Announces Unfortunate News  |url=https://www.vipsg.fr/news/marco-asensio-announces-unfortunate-news-258225/ |access-date=1 May 2025}}</ref>

In August 2025, Asensio was first romantically linked to influencer Lavinia León.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.elmundo.es/loc/famosos/2025/08/06/68933110fc6c830a3f8b4597.html |title=Marco Asensio, de nuevo enamorado: quién es la influencer con la que el futbolista recorre la costa italiana |date=6 August 2025 |access-date=28 September 2026 |newspaper=El Mundo |language=es}}</ref> On 28 September 2026, they announced via Instagram that they are expecting their first child, a baby boy.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.eleconomista.es/informalia/famosos/noticias/14017112/09/26/marco-asensio-y-lavinia-leon-esperan-su-primer-hijo-en-comun-la-familia-crece.html |title=Marco Asensio y Lavinia León esperan su primer hijo en común: "La familia crece" |date=28 September 2026 |access-date=28 September 2026 |newspaper=El Economista |language=es}}</ref>
